topics.topic: Whether record_change should reject or reuse an existing equal StoredValue identity
questions: Must an existing StoredValue identity raise StoreInternalError as an identity already present for an immutable record, or must an equal existing StoredValue be reused and returned? The invariant-error passage must exclude this StoredValue case, or the reuse passage must change.

judgement.why: This asks the same question about the same unchanged passages as P1.

precedent.topic: Behavior when recording an existing StoredValue identity
quotes: A StoredValue whose value_id already exists is not written again and the existing record is returned in its place, since equal values share one identity; spooled files must already be published in the run's spool by spool_file before the change that writes their SpooledFile records.

Any other broken invariant (a linked record missing, an identity already present for an immutable record, a status change from a status the change does not start from) or a failed transaction raises StoreInternalError with nothing written.
precedent.why: The specific StoredValue rule requires returning the existing record without rewriting it, while the phrase “Any other broken invariant” excludes that stated special case.

topics.topic: Whether an over-ceiling list counts as delivered without actual delivery or must be measurable as considered for delivery on the first passage
questions: Must an over-ceiling list be considered delivered despite not actually being delivered, or must the first passage allow measurement of lists considered for delivery?

quotes: only a list that is delivered, to a node or a flow output, is measured, and an output no edge takes fails nothing;
every delivered list of a mapped node MUST be measured before any of them is delivered or written, and when one exceeds the ceiling none of them is delivered, to a node or a flow output;
judgement.why: The first passage permits measurement only of a list that is delivered, while the second requires measurement before delivery and says an over-ceiling measured list is never delivered.

topics.topic: Whether Origin validation takes precedence over method and path routing errors
questions: For a non-POST request to MCP_ENDPOINT_PATH carrying an Origin header, which status must be returned: 405 or 403?
For a request to another path carrying an Origin header, which status must be returned: 404 or 403?

judgement.why: This asks the same unchanged question about the same passage as P7.

precedent.topic: Precedence of Origin validation versus path and HTTP method routing errors
quotes: Only a POST to the path equal to the imported MCP_ENDPOINT_PATH constant reaches answer_request; any other method on that path is answered 405, any other path 404, and a request carrying an Origin header 403, each without a body and without calling answer_request;
precedent.why: The Origin condition is unconditional, while 405 is limited to the correct path and every other path receives 404.

topics.topic: Whether response-id recovery requires reading the body when size or token validation fails
questions: Must the body be read to recover the response id even when the size or token check fails, or must responses to those failures use null without reading the body?

judgement.why: This asks the same unchanged question about the same passages as P4.

precedent.topic: Whether size or token refusals must leave the body unread with a null id or may parse it to recover the id
quotes: The body is one JSON-RPC 2.0 message, read only after the size and token checks.
The id of every response is the body's id member when the body is one JSON object whose id is a string or an integer, and null otherwise; reading it checks nothing and decides nothing.
precedent.why: The body is not read before size and token checks, so refusals at those checks cannot recover its id and use null.
